Uniform, Exponential and Normal side by side.

Repeated random samples of 50 goalkeepers; each contributes one x̄; sampling distribution tightens with n (σ/√n).
Center = point estimate; expanding margin of error; ME = critical × SE.
Three questions for every CI problem.
Five targets with soccer contexts: p (grass preference), p1−p2 (keepers vs outfielders), μ (reaction time), μ1−μ2 (training groups), paired.

scenes.description: Dot plot of sampled reaction times with x̄ and ±s; t*_{n−1} explained; SE = s/√n.
t vs Normal: heavier tails at small df, converging at large df.
z-table = left cumulative area; t-table = critical value for a chosen upper-tail area and df.
95% two-sided → .025 column; 90% → .05 column; row df = n − 1 (illustrated with df = 35).
One-sided bounds: lower bound to +∞ (α=.10 in the lower tail), upper bound from −∞.
Two independent training groups; difference of means; SE from s²/n of each group; Welch df; zero reference.
Same goalkeepers before/after a reflex drill; per-player differences d; one-sample interval on d̄.
n vs E curve (n ∝ 1/E²), p̂(1−p̂) maximised at 0.5, round up, worked n = 9604.
CI question vs test question.
H0 (default, equality) and Ha (<, >, ≠); alternative chosen before seeing data.

Four-column condition checklist filled as narrated.
